name: Pul
overview: Pul was a male king identified in Scripture as the King of Assyria. His role is specifically noted in 2 Kings 15:19, where he is mentioned in connection with the history of Israel and its neighbors. Beyond his kingship, no additional personal details such as tribe or family are recorded.
namesAndTitles: The name 'Pul' is used as a proper name in the biblical text without a given meaning. He is also referred to by the title 'King of Assyria,' which straightforwardly indicates his royal position and dominion over Assyria as stated in 2 Kings 15:19.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture does not record any family relationships for Pul beyond his designation as King of Assyria. No further relational information is provided in the biblical text.
scriptureSignificance: Pul's significance lies in his role as the Assyrian monarch during a critical period in Israel's history, as noted in 2 Kings 15:19. His kingship represents the Assyrian influence and interaction with the kingdoms of Israel and Judah. Although limited details are given, his mention underscores the geopolitical realities faced by God's people during the divided monarchy.
